Let G be a simple algebraic group of adjoint type over the algebraic closure
F p of a finite field Fp of prime order p, and σ a Frobenius map (that is, a surjective
                                                                 ′
homomorphism such that Gσ = CG (σ) is finite). Then G = Op (Gσ ) is a finite group
of Lie type. For a maximal σ-stable torus T of G, let N = NG (T ) ∩ G. Assume also
that G is simple and G ∼   ̸ SL3 (2). Does there always exist x ∈ G such that N ∩ N x
                            =
is a p-group?                                                             E. P. Vdovin
  ∗ A definitive answer for a stronger question on the size of a base has been obtained
in (T. C. Burness, A. R. Thomas, J. Algebra, 619 (2023), 459–504), which implies the
following answer (in the notation therein): there is x ∈ G such that N ∩ N x is a
p-group if and only if (G, N ) is not one of the following: (L3 (2), 7:3), (U4 (2), 33 :S4 ),
(U5 (2), 34 :S5 ).
